title.narrative: National Road Development Project

description.narrative: The proposed project in aligned with the ADB's Strategy 2030, which provides a special attention for the needs of landlocked economies and supports improving regional connectivity and competitiveness by addressing cross-border infrastructure needs. It is also in consistent with ADB's CPS, 2019-2023, for Uzbekistan. The CPS supports Uzbekistan's pursuit for improved quality of peoples' lives and creation of jobs through prioritizing regional cooperation and integration along with private sector development, and reduction of economic and social disparities. It advocates (i) accelerating economic growth through continuing interventions in the transport sector focusing on cross border roads that facilitate development of CAREC transport corridors; (ii) improvement of the growth inclusiveness and sustainability by enhancing employability of the population through skills development and strengthening climate change resilience; and (iii) leveraging regional cooperation by developing regional transportation links and accompanying logistics.

Status of Implementation Progress: Subproject 1 (Reconstruction of the national road between Derbent and Denau in Surkhandarya, 106 km):
"As of 25 November 2024 Engineer's report presented during the MTR mission, physical progress of the civil works was at 30.86% for Lot 1 (31.16 km), 31.72% for Lot 2 (31.60 km), and 6.12% for Lot 3 (43.63 km), all significantly behind targets of 82.26%, 76.38%, and 62.48%, respectively. The contractor made notable progress from July to November 2024, following minimal progress during March to June 2024. Reasons for delay noted in the latest Engineer's report during the MTR were (i) delays related to land acquisition with delayed payments to owners, (ii) cash flow issues, (iii) unresolved issues with utility relocation, (iv) changes in work volumes, and (v) tree felling and replanting including delayed permission for cutting down and replanting trees. Most notable issue for Lot 3 is that the Contractor has no access to 79% of the project.
Subproject 2 (Reconstruction of A380 Highway between Bukhara and Gazli, 87 km):
"As of 27 November 2024 Engineer's report presented during the MTR, physical progress reached 100.00% with financial progress at 85.7%, with contract duration fully elapsed and As-Built drawing submission, which is a prerequisite for TOC, is reported at 95% completed. Essential works to open the 4-lane road to traffic and issue the TOC were completed by February 2024, and miscellaneous works were completed by April 2024. On 20 September 2024, following site inspections, the signed Act of Working Committee with all the comments was submitted to the Employer for their further processing and preparing necessary documents for the State Acceptance Committee, date for which is to be announced yet.
Rural Roads (RR):
"RR in Bukhara. The reconstruction of 54 km of Rural Roads in Bukhara region signed on 14 March 2024 with the incumbent contractor (CR20BGC) for Subproject 2 with a completion date of 30 Jun 2025 for $14.4 million. Of which, $4.53 m (31.45%) has been disbursed as of 1 December 2024. The Rural Road work progress is behind the Work Programme due to delays in construction of bridges, culverts and concrete pavement. The physical progress was 27.9% against the planned 60.0% as per the Work Programme reported during the MTR mission. Key issues noted by the PMCS during the Mission Team's visit to the project site on 29 November 2024 are (i) poor work management, (ii) insufficient quantity of materials and equipment, (iii) delays in material supply, and (iv) insufficient quantity of manpower. To catch up the progress, the contractor has been requested to have a solely dedicated project manage on site, increase manpower, deploy additional equipment, streamline material supply, and arranging two-shift work schedules as also recommended by the Engineer. On 21 October 2024, the Contractor submitted revised Work Programme considering the current work progress. The Programme was reviewed by the Engineer and submitted to the Employer on 22 October 2024. However, the Employer declined the revised Programme requesting to follow the original Programme and ensure the work progress by taking additional measures.
"RR in Surkhandarya. The reconstruction of 52.9 km of Rural Roads in the Surkhandarya region was signed with the incumbent contractor for Subproject 1 (Lankaran Yol Tikinti OJSC) on 1 Mar 2024, with a completion date of 30 June 2025 for $8.7 million. As of 1 December 2024, $1.21 million (13.96%) has been disbursed. The implementation of the RR has been affected by the incumbent contractor, whose performance on the main 106 km road has been delayed significantly. The Mission will review the progress at site and agree with the EA on a recovery work program to complete the implementation in time.
